before: Keep raw meat refrigerated at 40°F / 4°C or below; thaw frozen meat in the refrigerator. Prepare ready-to-eat vegetables with clean tools, then keep them apart from raw meat and its utensils.

troubleshooting.problem: Tortilla strips fall apart before the skillet is ready
troubleshooting.cause: Forceful stirring or prolonged cooking after they have softened.
troubleshooting.fix: Stir gently once the strips are added and serve when the vegetables and meat have finished; strips already dissolved cannot be restored.

substitutions.effect: Keep the full measured amount and cook to 165°F rather than the beef endpoint; do not treat the same clock as proof.

after.timing: The inherited 30-minute plan includes about 15 minutes preparation and 15 minutes stovetop cooking. Onion/meat cooking precedes the 4–5-minute squash and approximately four-minute sauce first checks. Pan loads, vegetable size and meat temperature can extend this plan.
after.storage: Refrigerate perishable leftovers in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Use within 3–4 days or freeze promptly; follow any shorter remaining limit on prepared components. Reheat cooked meat, rice or casserole portions to 165°F / 74°C throughout. Tortilla strips soften further during storage; reheat the mixture evenly before adding a fresh garnish.

sources.title: Clean Food Crush — Chopped Enchilada Skillet

exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

Tortilla strips soften into the enchilada sauce while the vegetables keep some texture. Break up the meat finely and bring the finished mixture to a steady simmer before adding the cheese.

## Directions

1. **Cook:** Heat oil in large skillet on medium; add onion & beef. Saute until meat is almost done, then add both squash – cook another 4-5 minutes.

2. **Continue:** Add spices, fresh corn, beans, tortilla strips, and enchilada sauce. While gently stirring, let heat to a nice bubbly consistency – about 4 more minutes. Cook ground beef to 160°F / 71°C or ground turkey to 165°F / 74°C before serving.

3. **Continue:** Top with cheese & cilantro/green onions if desired.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

Tortilla strips soften into the enchilada sauce while the summer squash keeps some texture. Break up the meat finely, then stir gently once the strips are added so they remain recognizable. The optional cheese finishes the hot skillet without changing its full sauce and vegetable base.

## Directions

1. **Cook meat and onion:** Heat avocado or olive oil, yellow onion, and ground grass-fed beef or ground turkey in a large skillet over medium heat, adding the oil first, then the onion and meat. Break the meat into small pieces and sauté until nearly cooked. Choose a skillet with stirring room for the vegetables, beans, tortilla strips and sauce as well; divide all ingredients proportionally among additional pans or complete batches if needed.
2. **Add squash:** Add medium yellow squash and medium zucchini. Cook for another 4–5 minutes as a first check, stirring, until the vegetables begin to soften.
3. **Simmer:** Add ground cumin, paprika, garlic powder, sea salt, freshly ground black pepper, fresh corn kernels, cooked black beans, sprouted corn tortillas, and enchilada sauce. Stir gently to coat the tortilla strips and heat to a steady bubbling consistency, checking after about 4 minutes. Continue until the squash is tender and representative ground-meat portions reach 160°F / 71°C for beef or 165°F / 74°C for turkey. Stir for even heating; the first-check clock is not the endpoint. Taste only after the meat has finished cooking.
4. **Finish:** Finish with grated mozzarella or Colby Jack (if using) and fresh cilantro or green onions (if using). If choosing cheese, spread its full listed amount across the cooked mixture and allow it to soften. Serve promptly.
